Stand down on new credit spreads today or push DTE past the yield/war window. Cash is a position.

focus.jnote: The backdrop stays hostile to premium sellers. The 10-year Treasury yield is near ~5.12–5.16%, its highest since 2007, after strong S&P Global PMIs and a weak $70B 5-year auction pushed yields to multi-decade highs; markets now price ~64–70% odds of another Fed hike in October. Thursday the S&P 500 closed roughly flat (~7,704) and the Dow eased ~0.3%, with the Nasdaq marginally green as Meta rebounded. The US–Iran war keeps crude elevated near $93 (off recent ~$100 highs) as Hormuz flows stay disrupted — a persistent inflation feed. This is a rising-rate, war-overhang tape — not one to sell fresh spreads into.
focus.notdown: Generic pharma / breakout momentum (AMRX) is the one boarded bullish name still holding a bid — it broke to fresh 52-week/all-time highs on a string of FDA generic approvals (Somatuline/lanreotide, iohexol) and has held its breakout 3 sessions above the ~$19.10 pivot on 3.0x volume. But be honest: liquidity is NOT verified (one-sided/unquoted ATM), and heavy insider selling plus a “significantly overvalued” tag are hanging over it. Watch, size small, confirm liquidity at 9:35.
focus.notup: Rate-sensitive growth & chips stay the pressure point — higher yields hit long-duration names hardest. On the bearish board, SCHL gapped down ~12% on an earnings double-miss, but its reaction-day volume was essentially zero (0.01x, far below the 1.3x bar), so the “gap” isn’t confirmed by real participation — selling a bear call there is low-conviction. Shorting into a possible relief bounce carries squeeze risk too — the disciplined answer is to sell nothing new today.
focus.why: Why RED? Composite ~63 (deep WARM) and P(≥1% gap) ~39% is above the 35% trigger — either alone locks out GREEN. More important than the numbers: a bond sell-off to 2007-high yields plus a live US–Iran war and $93 oil is an open-ended, two-headed macro shock that can gap the whole tape on the next auction, data print, Fed comment or Hormuz headline. And the board itself is flawed: SCHL’s gap has near-zero volume confirmation and AMRX’s liquidity is unverified. Stand down on new credit spreads, or push DTE past the yield/war window and cut size hard. Cash is a position today.

setups.read: The scanner boarded SCHL Type A on a post-earnings gap DOWN and copies it through at Grade A+ (verbatim). Scholastic missed on both lines — adjusted loss of $3.63/sh vs ~−$3.42 expected, and revenue $216.8M vs ~$224.7M — and the stock fell ~12.4% after-hours to ~$30.5 from the $34.86 close. Honest red flags the scanner itself raised: reaction-day volume was ~0.01x the 50-day average, far below the 1.3x confirmation bar, so the gap lacks real participation, and there are NO S/R layers within 12% of price — nothing between the stock and a short call strike. Options-implied move was ~11.2% vs the realized ~−12.1% gap; ATM spread $0.05 screened OK but OI was not returned — verify manually. Next earnings ~Dec 24 is outside DTE. A textbook Type-A miss, but the near-zero volume and empty S/R stack make it a stand-aside on a RED day.

setups.read: The scanner boarded AMRX Type C on a 52-week/all-time-high breakout that has HELD 3 sessions above the ~$19.10 pivot; it copies through at Grade A. Honest red flags: the scanner shows only 1 S/R layer (pivot −4.5%), liquidity NOT verified — ATM market one-sided/unquoted, and outside sources flag heavy insider selling and a “significantly overvalued” tag. Next earnings ~Oct 29 is roughly 24 days out — near the edge of a 14-DTE window, so keep the spread short. It’s the one boarded bullish name still holding a bid, but the thin S/R stack and unverified liquidity argue for caution.
setups.check_note: On a RED day, half size at most or stand aside. Run 4-VAL at 9:35: price > Thu close (~$19.81), > today’s open, upper third of range. risks: Bond yields — 10Y near ~5.12–5.16%, highest since 2007 — driven by strong PMIs, a weak 5-year auction and record diesel prices. Any further spike hits rate-sensitive growth hardest and is the day’s number-one thing to watch.

Rate-hike repricing — markets now price ~64–70% odds of another Fed hike in October and ~48% in December, with several officials sounding hawkish. A hot data point or Fed comment would compound the sell-off.

US–Iran war & Strait of Hormuz — oil is elevated near $93 with Hormuz flows disrupted and Tehran rejecting a ceasefire. Any escalation sends crude (and inflation fear) vertical — the week’s biggest tail.

SCHL gap has no volume confirmation — the double-miss gapped it ~12% down, but reaction-day volume was ~0.01x average and there are no S/R layers within 12%. Run 4-VAL at 9:35; the empty stack means a bear call has nothing to lean on.

AMRX liquidity unverified — the breakout has held 3 sessions on 3x volume, but the ATM market is one-sided/unquoted and insiders have been net sellers. Confirm OI ≥ 500 and bid-ask ≤ $0.10 before any entry, and mind the ~Oct 29 earnings near the DTE edge.
